Context/Background: Renal cell carcinoma with sarcomatoid features (sRCC) is a highly aggressive tumor type yet preferentially responds to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). sRCC is unique in its ability to develop from various epithelial RCC subtypes, most frequently ccRCC, and sarcomatoid features typically exist as foci nested within an epithelioid RCC. Sarcomatoid clones are thought to arise from transformation of an epithelioid RCC cell through epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT).To better understand microenvironmental mediators of the paradoxical immune sensitivity of sRCC, we performed single-cell analyses of human sRCC tumors compared against clear cell RCC (ccRCC), with validation spatially and in bulk transcriptomic datasets totaling over 3,000 RCC tumors.
Prompt: Gene expression counts were aggregated by case and differential expression analysis on pseudobulked counts was performed. Based on the differential gene expression results, run GSEA on hallmark genesets, and provide a brief discussion of pathways important in the sRCC vs ccRCC context. From the top 20 differentially expressed genes, prioritize 5 genes and discuss their possible roles in tumorigenesis and sarcomatoid transformation.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Differential expression on pseudobulked single‐cell profiles compared sarcomatoid RCC (sRCC) versus clear cell RCC (ccRCC).  Gene expression counts were aggregated by case and tested for log2 fold‐changes with FDR.  The analysis is on human primary tumors; assay details beyond pseudobulk RNA‐seq are not specified.

Keywords  
• EMT (epithelial–mesenchymal transition)  
• ECM remodeling  
• Immune signaling  
• Sarcomatoid transformation  
• Cell–matrix adhesion  

Candidate Genes  
CD44, SEMA3C, TFAP2A, DCBLD2, PTPRH  

Pathway Enrichments  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: up 9, down 3 of 12 total (ratio 3.0 up:down)

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP)  
| Theme                                 | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                   |  
|---------------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|  
| Epithelial Mesenchymal Transition     | Up        | MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, COL12A1, BGN,… CD44,…    |  
| KRAS Signaling Dn                     | Up        | NOS1, PCDHB1, THRB, TEX15, IGFBP2,…        |  
| Myogenesis                            | Up        | BDKRB2, TNNT1, PVALB, NOS1, SOD3,… TPM2,…  |  
| Apical Surface                        | Up        | SHROOM2, EFNA5, SRPX, THY1, DCBLD2,…       |  

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (DOWN)  
| Theme                                 | Direction | Leading Genes (excerpt)                   |  
|---------------------------------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|  
| TNF-α Signaling via NF-κB             | Down      | KLF2, NFKBIA, TNIP2, FOSB, IER2,… JUN, MYC |  
| Interferon Alpha Response             | Down      | TRIM21, HERC6, LAMP3, ELF1, ISG15,… IRF7   |  
| Myc Targets V2                        | Down      | NIP7, IMP4, GRWD1, CDK4, HK2,… MYC         |  

Brief Analysis  
EMT emerges as the dominant up‐regulated program (NES 5.49, FDR 2×10⁻⁶), reflecting sarcomatoid clones adopting mesenchymal traits and ECM remodeling (collagens, integrins, fibronectin).  KRAS‐Dn and Myogenesis signatures also score high, suggesting cytoskeletal reorganization and contractile module activation.  “Apical Surface” up‐regulation may capture altered polarity in transformed epithelioid cells.  Conversely, down‐regulation of TNF-α/NF-κB and interferon–α response hints at suppression of classical inflammatory pathways in the mesenchymal niche.  Overall, sRCC up‐shifts migratory/ECM programs while dampening specific immune‐signaling axes.

Targeted Subset: EMT  
Filtering the full GSEA output on “Epithelial” reveals a highly significant EMT hallmark (NES 5.4927, FDR 1.98×10⁻⁶) with leading‐edge genes including MGP, COMP, IGFBP2, multiple collagens and CD44—consistent with a switch to mesenchymal and ECM‐remodeling states.

Key Genes (top 20 DE → prioritize 5)  
Upward direction indicates higher in sRCC versus ccRCC; downward indicates lower.

Up‐regulated (sRCC)  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function (summary)                                                                                                                                           | Pathway(s)                       |  
|---------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|  
| CD44    | Up        | HA receptor driving cell–matrix adhesion, migration, EMT; implicated in stemness and ICB response.                                                               | EMT, ECM remodeling              |  
| SEMA3C  | Up        | Secreted semaphorin that modulates cell motility and angiogenesis; can promote invasive phenotypes.                                                              | ECM remodeling, guidance cues    |  
| DCBLD2  | Up        | Cell‐surface scaffold that regulates growth factor signaling and wound‐healing programs; linked to EMT and motility.                                               | Apical Surface, EMT              |  
| TFAP2A  | Up        | Transcription factor that drives proliferation and differentiation programs; can regulate EMT‐related target genes.                                                 | KRAS Dn signature, transcription |  
| PTPRH   | Up        | Receptor‐type tyrosine phosphatase modulating RTK pathways; may influence cell–cell adhesion and EMT signaling.                                                   | ECM/integrin signaling           |  

Down‐regulated (ccRCC‐biased)  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function (summary)                                                                                                                                           | Pathway(s)                       |  
|---------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|  
| EPO     | Down      | Erythropoietic cytokine often high in ccRCC; reduced in sarcomatoid component, indicating lineage shift.                                                          | Hypoxia/EPO signaling            |  
| BIRC7   | Down      | Inhibitor of apoptosis; loss may reflect altered survival signaling in mesenchymal cells.                                                                           | Apoptosis regulation             |  
| HRH2    | Down      | Histamine receptor; its down‐regulation may reflect microenvironmental immune‐modulation.                                                                           | Immune‐signaling                  |  

Implications & Next Steps  
• EMT and ECM remodeling are central to sarcomatoid transformation, highlighting potential vulnerability to agents targeting collagen cross‐linking or integrin signaling.  
• Suppressed TNF-α/NF-κB and interferon pathways may contribute to altered immunogenicity; combining EMT‐targeted therapies with ICB could reinforce immune reactivation.  
• Functional studies of CD44, SEMA3C, DCBLD2, TFAP2A, and PTPRH in sRCC models to assess effects on motility, EMT markers, and ICB sensitivity.  
• Spatial transcriptomics to map these markers in situ, linking EMT foci to immune‐cell infiltration patterns.
